Dated this the 7th day of January, 2025 Nitin Jamdar, C. J.
Heard Mr. K. A. Salil Narayanan, learned counsel for the Appellant.
2.

By the impugned order, the learned Single Judge has incorporated a mandate under Section 3C of the National Highways Act, 1956 (Act of 1956), of giving a hearing to the objector who objects to the notification issued under Section 3 of the Act of 1956 on the ground that if the alignment is changed,
it would not be necessary to acquire the subject land.
According to the Appellant, there is no such requirement under Section 3C which will lead to setting aside notifications on the ground of non-compliance of principles of natural justice.

Learned counsel for the Appellant submits that it is a different question if the Court in writ jurisdiction directs the Project Director to give an opportunity to the objector but the language of Section 3C does not place any mandate on the authorities to give a hearing as to the objection to the alignment.
3. When the appeal came up for hearing on 24 June 2019, while admitting the appeal, an interim stay was granted after hearing both the parties.
Consequence of the interim stay was that the Appellant authority could go forward with the proceedings without adhering to the directions contained in the impugned order of giving a hearing.

After this order was passed on 24 June 2019,
the appeal has come up in 2025:KER:2534 regular course for hearing today.

4. Learned counsel for the Appellant states that pursuant to the interim order passed in the appeal,
the project has gone forward, the property is acquired, compensation is paid and the work is completed.
Therefore, by virtue of the interim order, the appeal in that sense, was allowed.
Perhaps that is the reason none appears for the Respondent.
